fact: The Bank of Ghana has started testing interoperability of CBDCs, stablecoins, bank accounts and mobile wallets with Rwanda and Nigeria, per Governor Asiama.
Governor Asiama said PAPSS has already been extended to mobile wallets along the Ghana-Nigeria corridor.
Governor Asiama described PAPSS as existing infrastructure in use by Ghana, extended to mobile wallets on the Ghana-Nigeria corridor.

Ghana News Agency reports the Bank of Ghana saying it is piloting cross-border interoperability with CBDCs, stablecoins, bank accounts and mobile wallets in the Ghana-Rwanda and Ghana-Nigeria corridors, with the aim of moving to live services.
Ghana News Agency reports the Bank of Ghana saying it has extended PAPSS to mobile wallets in the Ghana-Nigeria corridor.

MyJoyOnline reports Stanbic Bank Ghana, with Bank of Ghana approval, now offers direct yuan settlement via CIPS, with the service operational so individuals can make remittances, tuition and medical payments and businesses can pay China from cedi accounts.
The Bank of Ghana's Updated Guidelines for Inward Remittance Services set a framework for DEMIs and Enhanced PSPs partnering with Money Transfer Operators.
The Bank of Ghana's Second Deputy Governor says the e-cedi pilot includes work on cross-border settlement.
